chief_complaint: coughing up blood-streaked phlegm, worsening shoulder ache, and 6kg weight loss over 3 months
hpi_details: 3-month history of a persistent, changing daily cough that has recently started producing bright red blood-streaked sputum (haemoptysis) almost every morning. Over the same timeframe, has experienced an insidious, gnawing, constant ache deep in his right shoulder and upper back that radiates down the inner aspect of his right arm into the ring and little fingers. Has lost 6kg of weight unintentionally over the past 2 months along with profound loss of appetite. Over the past 3 weeks, his wife noticed his right eyelid drooping slightly and the right side of his face remaining completely dry when he sweats during gardening. Smoked 2 packs per day for 40 years.
ideas: thinks he tore a rotator cuff muscle in his right shoulder during gardening and strained his throat coughing
concerns: terrified the coughing blood and weight loss mean he has lung cancer spreading into his shoulder bones
expectations: wants an urgent chest CT scan, a bronchoscopy, and strong pain relief for his shoulder agony
pmh: smoker's cough for years, mild hypertension, no prior shoulder surgeries or TB
medications: amlodipine 5mg OD, paracetamol/codeine PRN for shoulder ache
social_hx: heavy current smoker (80 pack-years, smokes 40/day), drinks 14 units/week, retired dock cranesman

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of a Pancoast tumour is essential for timely staging, tissue diagnosis, and multidisciplinary management.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Urgent two-week wait fast-track referral to multidisciplinary lung cancer team (oncology, thoracic surgery, pulmonology), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: coughing up blood-streaked phlegm, worsening shoulder ache, and 6kg weight loss over 3 months

Key HPI features: 3-month history of a persistent, changing daily cough that has recently started producing bright red blood-streaked sputum (haemoptysis) almost every morning. Over the same timeframe, has experienced an insidious, gnawing, constant ache deep in his right shoulder and upper back that radiates down the inner aspect of his right arm into the ring and little fingers. Has lost 6kg of weight unintentionally over the past 2 months along with profound loss of appetite. Over the past 3 weeks, his wife noticed his right eyelid drooping slightly and the right side of his face remaining completely dry when he sweats during gardening. Smoked 2 packs per day for 40 years.

Objective/Exam findings: Perform targeted physical examination: right eye shows partial ptosis (drooping upper eyelid) and miosis (constricted pupil compared to left), plus ipsilateral facial anhydrosis on the right side (Horner's syndrome). Upper limb exam: wasting of the right intrinsic hand muscles (thenar and hypothenar eminences - T1 myotome) and sensory loss over the medial border of the right forearm and little finger (C8/T1 dermatomes). Check hand intrinsic power (finger abduction/adduction weakness). Chest exam: auscultation shows diminished breath sounds over the right lung apex. Check neck/supraclavicular fossae for palpable hard lymphadenopathy (Troisier's sign). Check fingers for digital clubbing. Urgent Chest X-ray: reveals a dense, ill-defined soft tissue mass density occupying the right apical lung field with destruction/erosion of the posterior aspects of the 1st and 2nd right ribs. Contrast-enhanced CT Thorax and Upper Abdomen: confirms right superior sulcus lung mass invading the lower brachial plexus (C8-T1 roots), stellate sympathetic ganglion, and adjacent rib cage.
Relevant background/PMH: smoker's cough for years, mild hypertension, no prior shoulder surgeries or TB
Current medications: amlodipine 5mg OD, paracetamol/codeine PRN for shoulder ache
common_misconceptions: Attributing shoulder pain to a musculoskeletal condition without considering an apical lung malignancy in a smoker.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Delaying staging and tissue diagnosis after identifying features of Pancoast syndrome.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Massive hemoptysis (> 300 mL/24h).
management_principles: Urgent two-week wait fast-track referral to multidisciplinary lung cancer team (oncology, thoracic surgery, pulmonology)

Diagnostic staging tissue acquisition: CT-guided percutaneous core needle biopsy of the right apical lung mass (preferred over bronchoscopy due to peripheral apical location) along with PET-CT scan to assess mediastinal nodal and distant metastatic spread
Address pain promptly with clinician-directed multimodal analgesia, taking account of respiratory risk, comorbidities, and monitoring needs.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 64M heavy smoker presents with 3-month haemoptysis, constitutional weight loss, right C8-T1 radicular shoulder/arm pain, and ipsilateral Horner's syndrome.
reference_soap.objective: Perform targeted physical examination: right eye shows partial ptosis (drooping upper eyelid) and miosis (constricted pupil compared to left), plus ipsilateral facial anhydrosis on the right side (Horner's syndrome). Upper limb exam: wasting of the right intrinsic hand muscles (thenar and hypothenar eminences - T1 myotome) and sensory loss over the medial border of the right forearm and little finger (C8/T1 dermatomes). Check hand intrinsic power (finger abduction/adduction weakness). Chest exam: auscultation shows diminished breath sounds over the right lung apex. Check neck/supraclavicular fossae for palpable hard lymphadenopathy (Troisier's sign). Check fingers for digital clubbing. Urgent Chest X-ray: reveals a dense, ill-defined soft tissue mass density occupying the right apical lung field with destruction/erosion of the posterior aspects of the 1st and 2nd right ribs. Contrast-enhanced CT Thorax and Upper Abdomen: confirms right superior sulcus lung mass invading the lower brachial plexus (C8-T1 roots), stellate sympathetic ganglion, and adjacent rib cage.
reference_soap.assessment: Pancoast Tumour (Superior Sulcus Bronchogenic Carcinoma - usually Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Squamous Cell or Adenocarcinoma) invading the brachial plexus and stellate ganglion causing Pancoast Syndrome and Horner's Syndrome. DDx: mesothelioma, apical tuberculosis / aspergilloma, cervical disc herniation / radiculopathy (ruled out by lung mass/haemoptysis/Horner's), thoracic outlet syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: Arrange urgent lung-cancer-pathway assessment and multidisciplinary review for diagnostic imaging, tissue diagnosis, staging, and treatment planning. Provide clinician-directed analgesia with monitoring. Seek emergency care for increasing haemoptysis, respiratory distress, hypoxemia, syncope, or chest pain concerning for PE or ACS.

learning_objectives: Correlate right shoulder ache and C8-T1 ulnar hand wasting with superior sulcus Pancoast tumour invading the lower brachial plexus
Identify the classical triad of Horner's Syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhydrosis) resulting from malignant stellate ganglion compression
Execute immediate two-week wait fast-track oncology referral while arranging CT-guided core biopsy over bronchoscopy for peripheral masses
Formulate aggressive neuropathic and opioid analgesic co-prescribing to alleviate severe brachial plexus cancer pain

teaching.one_liner: An apical non-small cell lung cancer that can invade the brachial plexus and sympathetic chain, causing shoulder pain and Horner syndrome.
red_flags: Severe hypoxemia, respiratory distress, or hemodynamic instability
Increasing haemoptysis, syncope, or chest pain concerning for PE or ACS

must_ask.say: How long have you had this cough, and are you coughing up blood streaks?
Do you wake up drenched in sweat at night or suffer from unexplained low-grade fevers?
Have you lost weight rapidly without trying over recent months?
Does the shoulder pain travel down your arm, and have you noticed hand weakness or numbness?
Have you noticed a drooping eyelid, a smaller pupil, or reduced sweating on one side of your face?
